instructions: Fresh review of each primary candidate: read dialogue first, then exact cards. Assess all six unchanged criteria and all coach-2.0 gates with turn-specific evidence. For pairs, show whether the Stance changes HOW A pursues the Drive in one interaction. Do not invent missing backstory or assume prior approval. Use the alternate only to assess meaningful differentiation. Report actual reservations. No writer scores or improvement claims are supplied.
productionStandard:
PRODUCTION STANDARD coach-2.0. Historical coach-1.0 acceptance is not coach-2.0 acceptance. Read the dialogue first and record what the spoken words establish before interpreting the card. Exact cards are already in this invocation: label internal-dialogue-first, never blind or human review. Do not invent a charitable backstory; harmless unspecified names/history are not defects. Fill coach2 for ORIGINAL dialogue in writer output and CANDIDATE dialogue in reviewer output. Copy the supplied dialogue hash for the text being assessed. Give concise actual turn evidence, not generic claims.
G1: legible immediate situation, wants/stakes; separate stated, ordinary inferred, and missing essentials. Identify first material defect or explicitly none.
G2: coherent facts, ownership, timing, language, knowledge; recognizable misunderstanding/revelation is allowed, unstated intervening events are not.
G3: assess all A1-B2, B2-A3, A3-B4, B4-A5 links. Vocabulary repetition alone is insufficient. Purposeful avoidance must read as behavior.
G4: B is a plausible participant with an intelligible practical/emotional position, not a contrived punchline cue. B can help, concede or solve.
G5: exact card changes A's choices. For pairs Stance changes HOW A pursues Drive and B responds to the merged behavior; neither card may be decorative.
G6: ending develops the same behavior using B4. Investigate if A5 would work after unrelated B4; more obstacles are not required for heightening.
format: five spoken ABABA turns, existing word/schema limit, no narration/coaching/truncation.
Every mandatory gate and transition is PASS, FAIL or UNCLEAR with evidence; UNCLEAR cannot be accepted. All gates pass AND total >=85 AND fidelity/response >=4 AND others >=3; preserve the six weights 30/20/15/15/10/10. A 5 is not merely presence. Totals are derived in code. Retain good originals; no rewrite quota. Review both alternatives for different tactics, relationships or pressure. Scene outline identifies roles, task, A want, B want, stakes, exact-card tactic and B's contribution; it is private planning evidence, not a substitute for missing spoken facts. Humour must come from sincere priorities and responsive choices, not stock hierarchy or unrelated slogans. Record actual weaknesses and reservations. Writer corrections target only rejected/materially changed scenes; preserve all accepted records and prior original assessments exactly. No coach-1.0 failure or exhausted allowance is erased by this separately versioned cycle.

cards.title: Top of the Ladder
cards.instruction: Carry yourself as the highest-status person present. Treat questions as requests for your approval.

cards.title: Technically, Yes
cards.instruction: Comply with every agreement in the narrowest possible way while insisting you honored it completely.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've approved my completed moving work. You asked for a box moved; this one is beside the van.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Can you move all twenty? That's what I meant.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Twenty is authorized. I'll place them beside the van; the revised quantity will be fully satisfied.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Can you put them inside the van?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Inside is approved. I'll stack all twenty just beyond the doors. Unloading them in any sensible order may be requested separately.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've approved the holiday watering as complete. The fern you pointed at has been watered.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Can you do every plant, every day until Sunday?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Daily coverage is approved: one teaspoon per plant through Sunday. Every word of your request will be met.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Can you use a full can on each and empty the saucers afterwards?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The quantities are authorized. I'll empty the saucers on Sunday; you requested daily watering, not daily emptying. Full compliance.

cards.title: Top of the Ladder
cards.instruction: Carry yourself as the highest-status person present. Treat questions as requests for your approval.

cards.title: One Thing Leads to Another
cards.instruction: Use each small problem to justify solving a broader, more disruptive problem.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've approved replacing the sink. That dripping tap has exposed an opportunity.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Can we just fit this washer? I've already bought it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Washer use is approved once the sink is out. Then we can replace the swollen worktop properly.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It runs under every cupboard.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Removal of the cupboards is authorized. You may start emptying them; with the kitchen bare, we can finally correct the whole layout.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: This cafe chair wobbles. I've approved taking all the chairs apart to check their joints.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Can we leave the others? I tested them. It's this one floorboard.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The chairs may remain intact. I authorize lifting the floor; your test has identified the real opportunity.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We're supposed to open in twenty minutes.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Closure is approved. You may put up the sign while I mark a new position for the counter. A bare floor lets us solve the queue as well.

cards.instruction: Carry yourself as the highest-status person present. Treat questions as requests for your approval.

cards.title: Make Them Your Deputy
cards.instruction: Get someone’s help by defining it as service under your direction.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I need help running the raffle. I've made you a deputy badge; you may put it on.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Can I be co-organizer? I sold all the tickets.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Your sales are approved. My deputy may arrange the prizes while I conduct the draw.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Can I announce the winners? I know most of the ticket holders.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Announcements are authorized. I'll draw and show you the number; you may add the winner's name once I've confirmed the ticket.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You may organize the picnic as my second-in-command. I've brought the packing list.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Can we share the work equally?

beats.speaker: A

beats.speaker: B

cards.title: Not Dismissed
cards.instruction: Keep someone present by treating departure as a privilege only you can grant.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll decide how we handle this. The shop's shut, but wait by the till until I dismiss you.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I've counted it. My daughter's waiting outside.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You can question the details after my decision. Bring her in. I can check the cash while you help with her homework.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: She's finished it. Our taxi's here.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then we'll finish your dismissal in the taxi. You may sit down, but tell him departure still needs my approval.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll decide how we handle this. Before you put your coat on, I'd like to formally conclude our coffee.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I only stopped for ten minutes. My bus is due.

beats.speaker: A

beats.text: The café's closing. They've asked us both to leave.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course. We'll wait outside together. Their permission to leave doesn't replace mine.

cards.title: Acknowledge the Disrespect
cards.instruction: Make someone apologize for the disrespect to your position, not merely for what happened.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll decide how we handle this. Your apology should mention interrupting the chair, not just spilling the tea.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm sorry about your trousers.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You can question the details after my decision. The trousers hold no office.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm sorry I interrupted you.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: 'Chair.' Let's repair the title while we're here.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll decide how we handle this. You told the trainees their head trainer was an idiot. I want an apology.
